source: due2-native (pins decisions/0016: an absent request field is missing, so each rule's part is opaque and completed alone; issues #56, #72)
notes: Authored for due2; no origin result. Both rules test the same target and the same assignee. When the request leaves one out, that field is missing (due2-profiles.md §3), so each rule's part is opaque: it shares no completion variable, and each rule is completed alone (decisions/0016 #2). The completions where one rule applies and the other does not give Permit and Deny, so scenarios 1 and 2 are Indeterminate, Deny..Permit, and unknown_parts names the missing field for both rules. Under decisions/0012 #1, which 0016 restricts to unresolved values, both rules read one variable, applied together or not at all, and scenarios 1 and 2 were NotApplicable: a verdict decided by cases over a value the request does not have. Scenario 3 is the same policy with every field named.

expected.why: The request names no target, so each rule's target part is missing and opaque, and each rule is completed alone (decisions/0016 #2): only the permission applying gives Permit, only the prohibition Deny, so Indeterminate, Deny..Permit.

The request names no assignee, so each rule's assignee part is missing and opaque, and each rule is completed alone (decisions/0016 #2): only the permission applying gives Permit, only the prohibition Deny, so Indeterminate, Deny..Permit.
Both rules apply; under invalid a T candidate and a T prohibition void the policy, each eliminated by the other with rule invalid (§6.2), and nothing remains.
